Here’s the gist, mate:

- Title/author/date: “Australia’s household income recession ends” by Leith van Onselen, Friday 12 December 2025.

- Key finding: Real per-capita household disposable income rebounded 2.5% in the year to September on a rolling four-quarter basis — the strongest pace since December 2021.

- Why it’s up: A mix of Stage 3 tax cuts, lower interest payments after rate cuts, and modest real wage growth.

- Reality check: It’s not yet back to the pre-pandemic trend. The decade’s growth in real per-capita income remains weak.

- Context compared: Real per-capita income growth this decade averaged about 0.51% per year, vs 0.95% in the 2010s “lost decade” and 3.19% during the commodity boom in the 2000s.

- Per adult nuance: Real income per adult has grown more slowly than per capita because immigration has boosted the adult population faster than the overall population. Since 2012, income per adult grew about 5.5% vs 7.7% per capita.

- Outlook: Without stronger productivity growth, real wages are expected to barely grow, keeping the risk of another “lost decade” in play.
